findings.description: The database username and password are rendered into EC2 user data and written to /var/www/inc/dbinfo.inc. EC2 user data is retrievable by processes with instance access and may be exposed through cloud control-plane access, creating a credential-disclosure risk.

The RDS instance sets publicly_accessible = true, assigning it a public network endpoint. Although the shown security-group ingress is VPC-scoped, this unnecessarily exposes the database to Internet-reachable network paths and weakens network segmentation.
The RDS instance explicitly sets storage_encrypted = false, leaving database storage and associated storage-level artifacts unencrypted at rest.

The policy grants s3:*, ec2:*, and rds:* on every resource. Attached to the role used by catalog_app_server, compromise of that instance would allow broad account-level data access and infrastructure modification, including likely privilege-escalation paths.
